definition: A system of data-manipulation rules (such as a computer's instruction set, a programming language, or a cellular automaton) is Turing complete if it can be used to simulate any Turing machine.
details: A system of data-manipulation rules (such as a computer's instruction set, a programming language, or a cellular automaton) is Turing complete if it can be used to simulate any Turing machine. This concept is used to determine the computational equivalence of different systems.
